name: dcf-aapl-2026-09-12
description: Illustrative AAPL-shaped context for tests. Statement figures are approximate; the news items and the model reply are synthetic and were written by hand because no API key was available when this fixture was created. Re-record against the live API with `npm run fixtures:record`.

profile.name: Apple Inc.
profile.description: Designs and sells smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services including the App Store, cloud storage, payments and subscriptions.

news.title: Apple unveils iPhone 18 lineup, keeps base prices flat
news.summary: Apple introduced four iPhone 18 models at its September event and held US starting prices unchanged from last year, while raising the Pro Max price by $100.

news.title: EU regulators open formal review of Apple App Store fee changes
news.summary: The European Commission opened a formal review into whether Apple's revised App Store terms comply with the Digital Markets Act, a process that can end in fines of up to 10% of global turnover.

news.title: 3 reasons Apple stock could soar this fall
news.summary: An opinion piece arguing new devices and services growth could lift the shares.

news.title: Apple in talks to expand Gemini partnership for Siri
news.summary: People familiar with the matter said Apple is negotiating a multi-year extension of its agreement to use Google's Gemini models in Siri. Terms were not disclosed and no deal has been signed.

news.title: Apple shares rise 2% as tech stocks rebound
news.summary: Apple rose alongside other large technology names as bond yields fell.

news.title: US judge sets 2027 trial date in DOJ antitrust case against Apple
news.summary: A federal judge scheduled the Justice Department's antitrust case against Apple for trial beginning in March 2027.

news.title: TSMC begins volume production of Apple A20 chips on 2nm
news.summary: TSMC started volume production of Apple's A20 processor on its 2-nanometer process, according to people familiar with the schedule.

news.title: Apple reports third quarter results
news.summary: Apple reported quarterly revenue of $97.9 billion, up 4 percent year over year, with Services revenue at an all-time high of $28.9 billion. The board declared a dividend of $0.27 per share.

modelOutput.headline: This valuation rests mainly on a stage one growth rate well above Apple's recent track record, and on a discount rate that determines most of the terminal value.
modelOutput.plainEnglish: A discounted cash flow estimate tries to guess what a company's future cash will be worth in today's dollars. Here the model assumes Apple's cash flow grows faster than it actually has in the past five years, and small changes to the discount rate used to bring future cash back to today's value swing the answer a lot.

assumptions.reasoning: The engine assumes 7.00% annual growth for the next stage, more than double the revenue growth and more than four times the free cash flow growth Apple has actually posted over the last five reported years.
assumptions.evidence: Revenue grew 3.28% a year and free cash flow grew 1.54% a year across the five annual periods provided.

assumptions.reasoning: A 2.50% long run growth rate sits inside the normal range associated with long run nominal economic growth, and is not itself unusual, but combined with the 8.40% discount rate it produces a gap that leaves the terminal period doing most of the work in the total value.
assumptions.evidence: Terminal growth is 2.50% versus a discount rate of 8.40%, and the engine reports terminal value equals 71% of enterprise value.

assumptions.reasoning: An 8.40% discount rate looks reasonable for a company with very low leverage, strong free cash flow margins, and no sovereign backstop needed, though there is no explicit risk free rate or beta shown in the context to fully confirm the figure.
assumptions.evidence: Net debt to EBITDA is 0.45x (strong) and free cash flow margin averaged 26.2% over the historical period, both indicating low balance sheet risk.

assumptions.reasoning: The free cash flow base of $98.80B matches the latest reported annual figure, but stock based compensation, a non cash add back, equals 13.1% of that free cash flow, which can flatter the cash generation picture used as the starting point.
assumptions.evidence: Stock based compensation is 13.1% of the latest reported free cash flow of $98.80B.

assumptions.reasoning: The 14.84B diluted share count used by the engine matches the most recent quarterly figure and continues a clear multi year trend of share count reduction from buybacks, so it is not a stale input.
assumptions.evidence: Diluted shares fell from 16.86B in fiscal 2021 to 15.00B in fiscal 2025 and to 14.84B in the latest quarter.

dominantSensitivity.explanation: With terminal value already reported at 71% of enterprise value, the discount rate has outsized leverage over the result, and a one percentage point move in a rate like this commonly shifts intrinsic value by 15 to 40 percent.

confidenceReasons: Stage one growth of 7.00% is well above the 3.28% revenue and 1.54% free cash flow growth actually reported over five years.
Terminal value makes up 71% of enterprise value, so the result leans heavily on assumptions about the far future rather than near term results.
Stock based compensation equal to 13.1% of free cash flow means part of the cash flow base is a non cash add back rather than distributable cash.
Balance sheet and buyback trends support the net debt and share count inputs, which adds some stability to the estimate.
